decisions.what: unattended default: environment = indoor bench/room ambient, 0-40 C operating, bare board, no ingress or vibration rating
decisions.why: Q1 of requirements section 9; brief names no environment. Most conservative common-practice choice for a USB-powered indoor sensor node; parts will still be picked at industrial -40..85 C grade where that is the stocked option, so the assumption cannot make the board wrong.

decisions.what: unattended default: Qwiic/STEMMA-QT downstream budget = 100 mA reserved on the 3V3 rail
decisions.why: Q2; brief does not budget it. 100 mA covers typical Qwiic sensor/display loads and still fits inside the brief's >= 300 mA LDO floor with margin for the on-board tens of mA, so it sizes the LDO and its thermals honestly without inflating the part.

decisions.what: unattended default: no hard per-board cost cap; minimize cost via JLC economy PCBA and Basic parts as the brief already directs
decisions.why: Q3; brief states no budget. Cost is already bounded by the brief's own Basic-parts-preferred rule; inventing a cap could force a worse engineering choice.

decisions.what: unattended default: the two 0.1 in headers (SWD, UART) ship UNPOPULATED - plated through-holes only, hand-solderable; only SMD parts go to JLC economy PCBA
decisions.why: Q4; brief says 'JLC economy PCBA for the SMD parts'. JLC economy assembly is SMT-only, so THT headers are BOM 'do not populate / customer supplied'. Standard practice for dev/sensor boards and it keeps the assembly quote in economy tier.

decisions.what: unattended default: ~35 x 25 mm is a SOFT preference, not an enclosure-driven hard cap; no HARD outline cap binds at P5
decisions.why: Q5; the brief says 'whatever an honest layout wants, roughly 35 x 25 mm or smaller' and names no enclosure. Confirms requirements.md section 5; placement must not optimize to fit an unearned number (the bb-buck failure mode).

decisions.what: unattended default: LDO = AMS1117-3.3 class in SOT-223 (JLC Basic, C6186); governing thermal design point is the brief's literal >=300 mA rated case (0.51 W), not the ~150 mA realistic load
decisions.why: research/ldo.md escalated the SOT-223-vs-SOT-23-5 tradeoff; research/power.md resolved it with numbers: AMS1117 Tj 71-86 C at 40 C ambient and <=115 C even in the 500 mA abuse case, while AP2112K-class SOT-23-5 (theta-JA 184 C/W) hits Tj 134 C at the rated case with no copper fix available. The Qwiic port is an unfenced 3V3 output, so the rated case is reachable in the field. Basic part, 1.1M stock, $0.20.

decisions.what: unattended default: a sub-6 V TVS clamping voltage is NOT a requirement; SMAJ5.0A/SMF5.0A-class (standoff 5.0-5.5 V, Vc ~9.2 V at Ipp) is accepted
decisions.why: research/protection.md flagged that no passive TVS clamps under 6 V. Nothing on VBUS is 6 V-rated: the only VBUS consumers are the LDO (AMS1117 Vin abs max 15 V), the input caps (16 V+ parts) and the PTC (16 V). Everything at 3.3 V sits behind the LDO. A ~9.2 V clamp during a surge is therefore inside every VBUS part's rating - the original <6 V framing was an over-tight derived spec, not a real one.

decisions.what: unattended default: NO series reverse-polarity element (no Schottky, no P-FET ideal diode) on VBUS
decisions.why: Two independent reasons, both recorded in research: (a) a compliant USB-C cable cannot present reverse polarity (protection.md), and (b) research/power.md computed the end-to-end dropout budget and found a series Schottky's 125-190 mV would consume the entire AMS1117 headroom at the 4.75 V source corner (+0.11 V worst-corner margin as designed). The unidirectional TVS already crowbars a reverse fault. Adding it would make the board worse, not safer.

decisions.what: unattended default: USB-C receptacle = 16-pin power-only part whose THT shield/mounting legs are accepted; JLC assembles it in the Economic PCBA tier
decisions.why: research/connectors.md correctly flagged that every 16P part in this class has THT shield legs and asked whether economy PCBA can place them. Verified directly on the JLCPCB part page for C165948 (TYPE-C-31-M-12): Assembly Process = SMT, Mount Type = Surface Mount Right Angle, and the part is listed as supported by BOTH Economic and Standard assembly. So the legs are not an assembly blocker. Part is JLC Extended - permitted, the brief names the connector.

decisions.what: unattended default: SHT4x on-chip heater (75 mA peak) IS budgeted in the rail tree at <=10% duty
decisions.why: research/power.md's call, accepted: including it costs nothing (peak +3V3 still 185 mA, 240 mA with 30% headroom, under the 300 mA LDO floor and at 39% of the 500 mA CC-blind USB entitlement), while omitting it would turn a documented firmware feature into a hardware ECO later.

decisions.what: unattended default: NRST tactile button - prefer the JLC Basic 5.1x5.1 mm part over the brief's smaller 3x2.5/4.2x3.2 mm size class if the layout has room; size class is a preference, Basic status and stock depth are the tiebreak
decisions.why: research/connectors.md Q2: the only Basic button is 5.1x5.1 mm (C318884, 962k stock, $0.02); the closest-size alternative carries a documented lib_pull symbol gotcha in this repo's own LEARNINGS. The brief never fixed the button size, and the board size is soft, so paying ~2.9 mm of edge for a Basic, gotcha-free part is the conservative trade. Architect may overrule at P2 if placement suffers.

decisions.what: unattended default: LED colours - user LED green, power LED red; both 0603, series resistors sized from the measured Vf band per colour
decisions.why: research/connectors.md Q3 left the assignment open. Red is the conventional power indicator and is the JLC Basic option with the low Vf band (1.8-2.4 V), which gives the largest resistor and the lowest current draw for an always-on LED. Green for the user LED is the conventional 'activity' colour; it is Extended in the KT-0603 family, which is acceptable at one extra unique part, and its 2.6-3.1 V Vf is fine from 3.3 V at a few mA.

decisions.what: research task block-mcu-1 closed over 1 unverified draft record(s): mcu-boot-strap-only-when-option-bytes-consult-pin
decisions.why: --accept-drafts: the slot ships without this knowledge

decisions.what: unattended default: BOOT0 gets a populated 10k pull-down on PA14 (pin 19, shared with SWCLK) - the board does NOT rely on the unverified factory-option-byte claim
decisions.why: The research record mcu-boot-strap-only-when-option-bytes-consult-pin was REFUTED by a fresh second reader: its load-bearing claim (factory 0xDFFFE1AA / nBOOT_SEL=1 makes the BOOT0 pin ignored) rests solely on a community.st.com forum page, and RM0454/AN2606 could not be acquired - st.com times out from this container (verified twice by curl, once by an agent). Rather than design on unverified knowledge, the board is made correct under EITHER option-byte state: a 10k pull-down guarantees BOOT0=0 at reset so the part boots main flash even if nBOOT_SEL=0. Cost is one 0402 resistor; 330 uA load on SWCLK is negligible to any debugger's push-pull driver, and the datasheet-confirmed internal pull-down on PA14 in debug mode already pulls the same way. This closes the gap without the source.

decisions.what: unattended default: I2C pull-ups are 1.5 kOhm (not the 2.2 kOhm the P1 fragment proposed)
decisions.why: The draft record sht4x-i2c-pullup-bus-cap was refuted for recommending 2.2k over its own declared 150-200 pF bus budget: UM10204 Eq 1 at tr=300 ns gives Rp(max) = 354/Cb[pF] kOhm, i.e. 1.77k at 200 pF, so 2.2k needs Cb <= 161 pF and misses the Fast-mode rise time on a cabled Qwiic bus. 1.5k holds the ceiling to 236 pF and clears both floors (967 Ohm from UM10204 Table 10 at 3.3 V/3 mA, 390 Ohm from the SHT4x datasheet). Value independently recomputed by a second reader. architecture/constraints.json and the P4 schematic must use 1.5k.

decisions.what: unattended default: AMS1117 SOT-223 tab is treated as VOUT (+3V3) - the thermal pour is a +3V3 pour, not an isolated island
decisions.why: The datasheet-extractor honestly refused to assert it: the 'TAB IS OUTPUT' label on page 1 sits against the TO-252 view, and no text restates it for SOT-223. Resolved as tab=VOUT because (a) the datasheet's own 15 C/W junction-to-TAB figure means the tab is the die-attach pad, which on this family's leadframe is the VOUT lead, (b) the KiCad standard symbol/footprint pair the librarian pulls ties tab to VOUT, so schematic and layout agree by construction, and (c) it is the safe direction either way: if the tab were floating, a +3V3 pour on it is still harmless, whereas assuming 'floating' and isolating the copper would throw away the thermal design the 0.51 W design point depends on. Flagged for the schematic reviewer to confirm against the pulled symbol.

decisions.what: unattended default: the SHT4x 20 V/ms VDD slew limit needs NO extra bulk capacitance - carried item CLOSED, not escalated
decisions.why: Two independent second readers read the SHT4x datasheet Table 4 slew row and quoted its condition verbatim: 'Voltage changes on the supply between VDD,min and VDD,max. Faster slew rates may lead to a reset' (min cell empty). That bounds supply changes DURING operation, not the cold-start ramp from 0 V - and a reset during power-on is the intended behaviour anyway (the part has a POR). In operation the 22 uF tantalum on +3V3 holds any load-step slew orders of magnitude below 20 V/ms. Adding bulk to slow a cold start would also fight the USB-C <=10 uF attach limit upstream. No hardware change; note it for bring-up.

decisions.what: unattended default: WAIVE schematic-review W1 (no ESD array on the J2 Qwiic SDA/SCL) - ship the board without a TVS/ESD array on the I2C bus
decisions.why: Product-scope connector checklist allows met-or-waived. Waived on four grounds: (a) the Qwiic/STEMMA-QT ecosystem norm (SparkFun/Adafruit reference boards) is a bare 4-pin JST SH with no array, so a user-facing part behaves as the ecosystem's users expect; (b) STM32G030 PA11/PA12 and the SHT40 both carry internal ESD structures and are 2 kV HBM rated, which is the standard handling rating for an indoor bench device; (c) the recorded environment is indoor bench/room ambient with no ingress rating, not a field-exposed port; (d) adding a 4-channel array now means a new Extended MPN plus setup fee, a fresh library pull and footprint verify, and re-opening a green schematic at P4 - real regression risk against a warning-severity, field-reliability-only exposure that cannot prevent bring-up. Recorded in reports/erc-waivers.md and shown at H2.

decisions.what: unattended default: CLOSE the carried verify item 'SHT4x VDD slew <= 20 V/ms vs AMS1117 startup ramp' (schematic-review W2) as accepted risk - no hardware change
decisions.why: Three findings close it. (1) PROVENANCE IS ON FILE, contrary to the reviewer's note: the 20 V/ms figure is research/records/sht4x-vdd-slew-power-up.yaml, sourced to research/sources/HT_DS_Datasheet_SHT4x.pdf p9 Table 4 and read visually TWICE (researcher + fresh second reader, maturity verified). The reviewer grepped parts/C2909890.json (the extraction JSON) and the LCSC PDF, which is a different artifact. (2) THE WORST-CASE NUMBER IS AN UPPER BOUND THAT CANNOT OCCUR: I_limit/C (~1 A into ~27 uF, 40-68 V/ms) assumes the LDO sources its full current limit into the output cap independently of its input. The AMS1117 is a series pass follower - during a cold start VOUT cannot rise faster than VIN minus dropout, so +3V3's edge is set by the USB source's VBUS ramp through C2 = 10 uF, not by the LDO's current limit. (3) THE NAMED FAILURE MODE IS BENIGN AT COLD START: the datasheet says only 'faster slew rates MAY lead to a reset'; the second reader explicitly flagged 'or hung until re-powered' as an unsupported clause the researcher added. A reset during the power-up ramp lands the part in exactly the state a power-up is supposed to produce - there is no state to lose at t=0. The limit's real bite is in-operation supply excursions and hot-plugging a DOWNSTREAM breakout onto a live Qwiic rail, which is the breakout's decoupling problem, not this board's. HARDWARE ALTERNATIVES REJECTED: a series R at U3 VDD to slow the local ramp is disqualified by the SHT4x on-chip heater (75 mA peak would drop 7.5 V across the 100 ohm needed for a 100 us tau); raising C3 above ~50 uF to force I_limit/C under 20 V/ms buys nothing against (2) and costs a part change on a green schematic. BELT AND BRACES (documentation, not copper): the firmware note 'issue an SHT4x soft reset (0x94) at init, per Sensirion's own recommended start-up sequence' goes into the design doc and fab/README, and the Qwiic hot-plug caveat is recorded as a known limit.

decisions.what: unattended default: carry a P9 REQUIRED check - CPL rotation must be validated for every polarized 2-pin part (D1 TVS SOD-123, D2 power LED, D10 user LED, C3 tantalum CASE-A), not only for J1
decisions.why: schematic-review OPEN item. decisions.md #13 carried a CPL rotation check for J1 alone; the KiCad<->JLC 0-degree-reference offset (reference/jlc_rotations.csv, LEARNINGS/S8) bites every polarized package, and a reversed tantalum on 3V3 or a reversed TVS on VBUS is a dead board, not a cosmetic error. dfm_check.py owns polarity/rotation validation - at P9 its findings for D1/D2/D10/C3 must be read explicitly and each confirmed against the footprint pin-1 marking, not just accepted as a count.

decisions.what: unattended default: P5 runs board_init --mounting-holes 4 --mounting-hole-fp MountingHole:MountingHole_2.2mm_M2 --margin 6 --outline auto; the four holes are explicitly RELEASABLE at P6 - the placement agent may move them with place_edit to the earned corners before board_edit --outline fit
decisions.why: Three linked calls. (1) HOLE SIZE: board_init's mounting-hole footprint was hard-coded to MountingHole_3.2mm_M3, but the brief and constraints ask for M2 (2.2 mm drill). I added an additive --mounting-hole-fp flag to board_init.py, default unchanged, so the M2 hole is stated rather than inherited (MountingHole_2.2mm_M2: NPTH 2.2 mm drill, 4.9 mm courtyard, which also serves the constraints' 4.0-4.5 mm annulus/head clearance). (2) MARGIN 6: --mounting-holes places holes at margin/2, so margin 6 puts the M2 centres 3 mm inside the edge - the standard M2 corner inset, and 1.9 mm of board between hole wall and edge. A smaller margin would push the hole courtyard across the board edge. (3) HOLES RELEASABLE AT P6: place_seed/place_anneal treat board_only footprints as immovable obstacles, so holes parked at the PROVISIONAL corners would fix the fitted bbox at the provisional size and defeat geometry-as-OUTPUT. They were auto-placed by a script at an arbitrary provisional corner, not by the owner, so the placement agent is authorised to move them with place_edit to the corners the earned layout wants - the agent-prompt rule against moving board_only refs exists to protect owner-placed mechanical fixtures, which these are not. Order follows the bb-mcu P6 recorded pipeline defect: place canonically, move the holes, board_edit --outline fit, and only THEN run the place gate (legality measures declared edges against the CURRENT outline, so gating before fit would spread the connectors to the provisional size).

decisions.what: unattended default: J1 USB-C footprint repaired at P5 - the four wide GND/VBUS pads restored to the vendor's own 0.60 mm land width, reopening the GND-VBUS gap from 0.100 mm to 0.200 mm
decisions.why: board_init's self-check DRC found two clearance ERRORS inside J1's own footprint: pad A1B12 [GND] vs A4B9 [VBUS] at 0.1002 mm and B1A12 vs B4A9 at 0.1000 mm, against the aiee_clearance_floor of 0.127 mm (JLC 2-layer 1 oz). J1 was never geometry-checked at P3 (fp_verify needs a datasheet-extract JSON and none exists for it). The librarian fetched the HRO Hroparts TYPE-C-31-M-12 drawing: its RECOMMEND P.C.B LAYOUT calls the four wide pads '4-0.60', i.e. 0.60 mm wide on a 0.8 mm pitch = a 0.20 mm gap, already above the floor. The pulled easyeda2kicad custom-pad polygons were the vendor's 0.60 mm, but carried a spurious 0.1 mm outline STROKE that inflated the effective copper to 0.70 mm and closed the gap to 0.100 mm. So this was a converter artifact, not a vendor deviation, and the fix RESTORES the manufacturer's land pattern rather than inventing a number: outer X vertices moved in by 0.05 mm per side on those four polygons only, pad centres / 1.30 mm length / the other 12 pads untouched. Contact tab is 0.20 mm wide (drawing callout 16-0.20+-0.05), so 0.60 mm still leaves 0.20 mm of fillet per side - the vendor's own allowance. Rationale recorded in the footprint descr, matching the P3 SHT40 die-pad precedent.

decisions.what: unattended default: P7 must hand-route the VBUS entry out of J1 - the 0.8 mm Pwr_0p8mm netclass cannot escape J1's 0.60 mm vendor pads on F.Cu at ANY placement, so route_critical owns it and Freerouting must not be asked to
decisions.why: The placement agent's route probe closed at 0.969 (62/64) and root-caused the two residuals: J1's VBUS pads are 0.60 mm wide with 0.20 mm gaps to their GND neighbours, so a 0.8 mm track (the VBUS netclass width rules_gen derived from the 1.5 A PTC-dwell case) cannot leave them on the top layer without breaking the 0.127 mm clearance floor - it is a geometric impossibility, not a placement defect, and no amount of re-placing fixes it. A via-in-pad escape to B.Cu was proven DRC-clean on a scratch copy; Freerouting cannot place via-in-pad, so this is route_critical's job before the autorouter runs. THREE THINGS P7 MUST WEIGH, in this order: (1) a short NECKED escape (fab-minimum width for ~1 mm out of the pad, widening to 0.8 mm once clear of the connector) is the ordinary way this is done and needs no via - but it violates the ERROR-severity aiee_pwr_width_VBUS rule, so taking it means a rule EXCEPTION with recorded evidence (the pad itself is 0.60 mm, so the 0.8 mm rule is already wider than the conductor the current must pass through), not a silent neck; (2) via-in-pad to B.Cu carves the B.Cu GND pour under the connector and JLC will wick solder into an unfilled 0.3 mm via on a mechanically loaded connector pad - if this route is taken it needs an order remark and a fab/README note; (3) the two VBUS pads are ganged, so each carries half the fault current. Do NOT resolve this by editing the netclass or the floor to make DRC quiet.

decisions.what: unattended default: J1 VBUS escape resolved as pour-carried copper (a measured third option), no rule exception and no via-in-pad
decisions.why: route_critical --pad-window measured J1 A4B9/B4A9 escape windows at 1.315 mm, comfortably above the 0.8 mm Pwr_0p8mm requirement, which retires the P6 premise that the escape was geometrically impossible - the impossibility applied to a 0.8 mm TRACK leaving the pad, not to the pad's available escape corridor. The F.Cu VBUS pours connect the pads with a solid zone connection and a ~1.45 mm fill band east of the pad column, so the conductor carrying the 1.5 A PTC-dwell fault current is WIDER than the 0.8 mm the rule asks for, not narrower. aiee_pwr_width_VBUS conditions on A.Type=='track', so zone fill is outside its scope by construction - the gate passes because no VBUS track anywhere is below 0.8 mm, not because a rule was relaxed. Neither P6 option was taken: no neck (so no ERROR-severity rule exception to record) and no via-in-pad on J1 (so no unfilled via in a mechanically loaded connector pad, and no JLC solder-wicking remark needed in fab/README). The two F.Cu VBUS pours are joined by a 0.8 mm B.Cu bridge on 2+2 vias placed in open pour with holes clear of every pad edge. VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, not taken on the router's word: plane_repair --flag-only on the final board reports VBUS as 1 electrical group (the two 8.4 and 7.8 mm2 F.Cu components joined through the bridge), and kicad-cli DRC reports 0 violations / 0 unconnected / 0 parity.

decisions.what: unattended default: the B.Cu VBUS bridge does NOT split the GND plane - verified on the final board, not inherited from the pre-bridge run
decisions.why: The 0.8 mm B.Cu VBUS bridge crosses the layer whose whole area is the GND pour, which is precisely the 'viasless pour-channel' blind spot the playbook lists as a router duty. The router's own plane_repair2 run was restricted to +3V3, so it never re-examined GND, and the only GND-clean evidence on disk (plane_repair.json: GND B.Cu 1 group, split False) predated both the snapshot restore and the bridge. I re-ran plane_repair.py --flag-only (never writes) on the final board: GND B.Cu = 1 group, split False, 813.2 mm2, 27 anchored components, 0 dead islands. The ground return is continuous under the bridge.

decisions.what: unattended default: U3 island U-slot obligation satisfied by the P6 outline - no new Edge.Cuts cut at P7
decisions.why: Edge.Cuts already carries two 5.5 mm slots from the right edge (y 36.85-38.05 and 44.95-46.15), making the sensor region a tongue with open air on three sides - which is what the B4 contract's 'milled U-slot around the island's inboard sides where the outline allows' asks for. No new cut means the outline did not change at P7, so gate place needed no re-run for outline reasons (it was re-run anyway for the copper hash). The rest of the B4 thermal contract was delivered by routing: exactly 4 necked crossings into the tongue (SDA 0.127 / SCL 0.127 / GND 0.127 / +3V3 0.150, the lawful minimum for that net), and zero copper and zero pour fill inside the tongue on both layers. Freerouting had routed SCL THROUGH the island as a fifth crossing; that pass was removed and the I2C trunk rebuilt on B.Cu.

decisions.what: unattended default: iter-2 route_auto placement_adjust_request judged premature and NOT escalated to the P7->P6 backward edge
decisions.why: The request (nets +3V3, /main/SDA, GND, VBUS; reason 'unrouted after 3 freerouting rungs') was emitted before stitch_vias and plane_repair had run, and on the 2-layer chain those two steps own three of its four nets - the autorouter was reporting work the chain had not yet done, not a placement defect. Finishing the chain plus point fixes closed all four nets: completion 1.0, 0 unconnected, gate drc_routed PASS 0/0. Taking the backward edge would have discarded a placement that passes gate place 0/0 in order to fix nets that were never stuck.

decisions.what: unattended default: starved_thermal on C11.1 and U2.4 cleared with same-net copper stubs into open fill
decisions.why: Both pads are geometrically capped at a single thermal spoke - the measured channels around them cannot host a second spoke lawfully at the 0.127 mm floor. The fix adds same-net copper into open fill rather than altering the thermal-relief geometry, so no zone parameter, netclass, .kicad_dru rule or gate definition was touched anywhere on this board (git confirms .kicad_dru and .kicad_pro are unmodified through all of P7). The pads are a decoupling cap ground and an MCU ground pin, both low-current: the stub restores the connection the DRC wanted without changing the pour's thermal-relief behaviour for reflow.

decisions.what: unattended default: the U1 tab pour lands at 113.2 mm2 contiguous (not the 600-1000 mm2 constraints target) and that is ACCEPTED - the declared dt_c 45 K is still met at 40.8 K rise
decisions.why: AREA, CORRECTED. The router reported 158.0 mm2 'connected'. That number is right for CURRENT and wrong for HEAT: plane_repair --flag-only on the final board shows the +3V3 F.Cu pour as four components (113.2 + 24.3 + 18.4 + 1.6 mm2) merged into one electrical group by 0.25 mm and 0.5 mm bridge TRACKS. A 0.25 mm track carries 0.3 A with a 13 mV drop but conducts essentially no heat, so the thermal spreader is only the contiguous component containing U1's tab: 113.2 mm2. Use 113 mm2, not 158, at P8. THERMALLY THIS STILL PASSES, and by the board's own declared criterion. Per knowledge record ldo-sot223-thermal-copper-sets-current, AMS1117 datasheet p5 Table 1 (1/16 in FR-4, 1 oz) measures 80 C/W for 100 mm2 top plus a backside pour - almost exactly this geometry (113 mm2 top; B.Cu GND pour measured 813.2 mm2 under and around U1). The record states explicitly that the spreading layer need not be electrically connected, so the GND pour counts as a spreader even though the recorded decision correctly forbids thermal vias and back-side +3V3. Tj = Ta + PD*thetaJA: governing rated case 40 + 0.51*80 = 80.8 C; realistic 0.26 W case 60.8 C; entitlement-abuse 0.83 W case 106 C - all under the 125 C limit, and the abuse case retains 19 C of margin. Crucially the RISE is 40.8 K against the constraints.json thermal[] declared dt_c of 45 K, so the check P8 actually runs is met with margin; the 600-1000 mm2 figure was the architect's MEANS to that end (it targeted Tj 71-76 C), not an independent requirement, and the earned 35.79 x 28.34 mm outline cannot fund it once the U3 island tongue, J1, the MCU, the headers and the VBUS pours are subtracted. Not silently accepted and not padded: the honest area is recorded, the arithmetic is shown, and P8 check_thermal recomputes it independently. Shrinking the U3 island void to buy pour area was rejected outright - the B4 isolation contract outranks the C obligation.

decisions.what: unattended default: g0-sense authors NO SPICE bench, so the sim gate is not applicable - recorded as a judgment, not left as a silent gap
decisions.why: The full-run recipe spawns sim-analyst 'for boards with nontrivial analog content', and the sim gate is conditional on a bench existing (gate.py --gate sim <dir>), so nothing is being skipped against the run contract. But an absence with no reasoning behind it is indistinguishable from an oversight, so here is the reasoning. Every block on this board is DC or digital: a fixed LDO, an MCU on its internal HSI16 with no crystal, an I2C sensor at 400 kHz, two indicator LEDs and passive protection. The wrong-value defect class that sim exists to catch (a 47k where 4.7k belongs) has no analog fragment to bite here - the value-bearing parts are the LDO caps, the two I2C pull-ups and the two LED series resistors, and all four were already sized against sourced numbers and re-checked by a fresh second reader at P2/P3 (I2C pull-ups revised 2.2k -> 1.5k against a UM10204 budget; LED resistors sized at the ~2 mA design point against the Vf bin spread; the 22 uF tantalum COUT is the AMS1117 datasheet stability requirement, not a free choice). The LDO loop itself is explicitly out of SPICE scope by policy - no vendor models are vendored - and its stability is a datasheet ESR-window requirement already met by the tantalum (knowledge record ldo-1117-family-output-cap-esr). Authoring a bench here would produce a testbench of generic model cards proving Ohm's law, which is ceremony, not evidence. The real verification for this board is the P8 layout suite: return path, current, decoupling, thermal and PDN all run against the actual copper.

decisions.what: unattended default: the check_pdn VBUS error was a real DATA gap in decoupling.json, fixed by adding the missing C1 association - not waived
decisions.why: check_pdn reported 'power rail VBUS (1.5 A) has no decoupling capacitors'. The observation was true of its INPUT and false of the board: check_pdn does not look at copper at all, it filters decoupling.json associations by rail, and decoupling.json listed only C2/C3/C10/C11/C13 - every IC decoupler, but not the connector-side bypass. constraints.json is explicit that C1 = 100 nF at the connector is the ONLY capacitance on VBUS ahead of the PTC (the USB-C 10 uF attach limit, TC2.0 Table 4-3), and I confirmed on the board itself that C1's pads sit on VBUS and GND. So the inventory was incomplete, and the honest fix is to complete it rather than waive a true-but-misleading finding. Added {cap C1, ic J1, pin A4B9, rail VBUS, value 100nF 50V X7R}. Measured BEFORE adding it, so as not to trade one finding for another: C1 is 5.52 mm Manhattan from J1's nearest VBUS pad, inside check_decoupling's 7.5 mm HF-class error threshold - and check_decoupling still passes afterwards, rating the loop at 5.32 nH. The error correctly downgraded to the warning 'VBUS has 1 cap but no bulk reservoir', which is the INTENDED design and not fixable: bulk on VBUS ahead of the PTC is forbidden by the USB-C attach limit, which is why the architecture put the 10 uF after the PTC on +5V instead.

decisions.what: unattended default: the check_current pour_neckdown finding on VBUS was a per-zone checker artifact - the real current path is >= 0.8 mm everywhere, verified independently by the orchestrator
decisions.why: The checker reported the VBUS F.Cu pour necking to 0.10 mm against a 0.800 mm IPC-2152 requirement at 1.5 A. The P8 fixer diagnosed it as an artifact of check_current.py running its erosion test per ZONE FILL (check_current.py:283) when planes_gen deliberately tiles a pour across abutting same-net zones at distinct priorities, so a tiling seam reads as a neck. I did not take that on the agent's word, because a genuine 0.10 mm neck in the board's only power trunk would be a serious defect. I re-ran the checker's own erosion test on the physical UNION of the VBUS F.Cu fills plus J1's VBUS pad copper: eroding by 0.4 mm - i.e. testing the full 0.800 mm requirement at the conservative 1.5 A fault basis - leaves pad A4B9 connected to all three of its vias in one region, and pad B4A9 connected to all three of its vias in another. The current path therefore satisfies IPC-2152 at 1.5 A with no neck at all. The narrowest real feature I could find in that copper is 0.680 mm (found by bisection), and when the region splits there, the severed 0.33 mm2 lobe contains NO via and NO pad - it is a dead-end lobe carrying no current. CONSEQUENCE: no correction to constraints.json was needed. The insufficient_transition_vias remediation doc names an inflated transient current_a as a known bad-input class and reserves that lever for the orchestrator, and VBUS's 1.5 A is indeed a fault-transient basis (the PTC dwells there for seconds; steady draw is <= 0.25 A) - but the board meets the declared 1.5 A requirement PHYSICALLY, so relaxing the input would have been unnecessary and would have weakened the record. constraints.json is unchanged.

decisions.what: unattended default: the two VBUS insufficient_transition_vias errors were fixed with real copper (2 vias -> 3 at each transition), not by relaxing the current basis
decisions.why: The remediation's fix ladder step 1 is to measure candidate room before acting, and the fixer did: cluster A at (28.075, 38.90) had 0 legal cells at the 0.2 mm netclass clearance and only 7 at the board's real 0.127 mm DRU floor, all 0.07-0.10 mm from D1's pad - too tight to use safely; cluster B at (28.075, 44.30) had 0 legal cells at any clearance, boxed in by R2's CC2 pad and hole-to-hole against the existing pair. Rather than stop at 'infeasible', the fixer re-arranged: moved one via and added another on a 0.4 mm B.Cu stub for cluster A, and extended the B.Cu bridge 0.9 mm to land a third via inside the existing bottom pour for cluster B (clearances 0.865/0.874 mm, hole-edge gap 0.600 mm). Both clusters now hold 3 vias, satisfying the >= 1 via per 0.5 A rule at the full 1.5 A basis. The remediation's traps were respected: no via was deleted to tidy a cluster, every new via bonds same-net copper on both layers (no dangling), and hole-to-hole against J1's THT shield-leg drills was computed by hand because KiCad DRC is blind to that case. check_current now returns 0 violations and drc_routed still passes 0/0.

decisions.what: unattended default: the 6 check_silk silk_misattributed WARNINGS are accepted and recorded, not fixed - and not waived either, since they do not fail the gate
decisions.why: R2, R1, C10, D2, R10 and D1 carry refdes text that sits 2-3 mm beyond its own pads and closer to a neighbour, so each reads as the neighbour's label. Three reasons to accept them. (1) KiCad's own DRC - the authoritative oracle after P7 - reports ZERO silk findings on this board; this is check_silk's stricter readability heuristic, and the gate treats it as warning severity for exactly that reason. (2) The alternative is measurably worse. P6 already fought this battle down from 13 silk DRC violations to 0, and it needed a new place_edit silk_clear op plus two library edits to do it. That phase also recorded, from a test on a copy, that re-running silk_place on the now-clean board APPLIES BEFORE IT REPORTS, does not roll back, and proposed moves that put D1's Reference back over J1's VBUS pad - trading warnings for real DRC errors. On a 35.79 x 28.34 mm board with 26 parts there is nowhere to move a 0603's refdes except over its own pads. (3) The board is JLC economy PCBA: the machine places the SMD parts, so refdes text serves human debugging and rework, where the part outlines and the assembly drawing disambiguate. Carried to P9/P10: note the crowding in fab/README so the owner is not surprised, and do NOT let a DFM pass 'fix' it by running silk_place.

decisions.what: unattended default: REVISING my earlier P8 stance on the 6 silk_misattributed warnings - they are now a REQUIRED P9 fix (place_edit move_text), not an accepted residual
decisions.why: The fresh-context verify-reviewer overruled the reason I gave, and it was right to. I accepted the warnings partly on the grounds that refdes text mainly serves human debugging and rework, and that the part outlines disambiguate it. The reviewer measured what actually happens after assembly: four of the six texts end up UNDER part bodies (R1 and R2 under J1's shell, C10 under U2, D1 inside U1's outline). Text under a component body is not ambiguous, it is invisible - which defeats the exact purpose I used to justify accepting it. So the finding is real and worth fixing. HOW IT MUST BE FIXED AT P9, and this is load-bearing: place_edit move_text on individual pin-locked labels ONLY, with a full kicad-cli DRC after each move. Do NOT run silk_place.py on this board - P6 recorded, from a test on a copy, that it APPLIES BEFORE IT REPORTS, does not roll back, and proposed moves that put D1's Reference back over J1's VBUS pad, i.e. it trades warnings for real DRC errors. Do not recreate kicad/silk_ops.json. If a given label has no legal destination on a 35.79 x 28.34 mm board, leaving that one is an acceptable outcome - but it must be the measured exception, not the default for all six.

decisions.what: unattended default: carry TWO more P9 obligations from the verify-reviewer - J3/J4 per-pin silk labels, and U3 added to the CPL rotation check list
decisions.why: (1) SILK PIN LABELS: architecture/blocks.md promises per-pin labels on the two 0.1 in headers (J3 SWD: GND/3V3/SWDIO/SWCLK; J4 UART: GND/3V3/TX/RX) and the board does not have them. These are the two connectors the OWNER hand-wires - the brief calls J4 a readout/logging header - so an unlabelled 4-pin row is a real usability defect and a wrong-way-round UART connection is the predictable consequence. Eight texts to add at P9 with place_edit add_text, DRC-verified, subject to the same 'no legal spot is an acceptable measured exception' rule as the refdes moves. (2) CPL ROTATION: decisions already carry a REQUIRED P9 check that CPL rotation be validated per polarized part for D1 (SOD-123 TVS), D2 and D10 (LEDs) and C3 (tantalum CASE-A), not just J1. The reviewer adds U3, the SHT40 in DFN-4 - a rotated DFN-4 sensor is as dead as a reversed tantalum and the package gives the pick-and-place no mechanical asymmetry to self-correct against. P9 must read dfm_check's polarity/rotation findings for D1, D2, D10, C3 AND U3 explicitly, each confirmed against the footprint pin-1 marking, never accepted as a count.

decisions.what: unattended default: carry a P10 ORDER REMARK - ask JLCPCB not to land break-off tabs on the SHT40 sensor tongue's outer edge
decisions.why: The verify-reviewer flagged that the tongue's outer face (x = 54.75, y 38.05-44.95) is a board edge JLC's internal panelizer may choose for break-off tabs or mouse-bites. That edge is the free end of a cantilever whose whole purpose is to hold the sensor thermally and mechanically isolated from the board; a tab landing there puts depanelization stress directly into the tongue root and leaves a rough breakout beside the sensor aperture. This costs nothing to prevent and cannot be fixed after the fact. It goes in the JLC order remarks alongside the Sensirion assembly rules already carried from P2 (no-clean paste, NO post-assembly board wash, no vapor-phase reflow, no hand rework of the sensor), and into fab/README so the owner can restate it if JLC comes back with a panel proposal.

decisions.what: unattended default: the P9 silk pass is a MEASURED PARTIAL and is accepted there - 4 of 8 header pin labels added, 2 of 6 misattributed refdes moved, DRC still 0/0/0
decisions.why: TASK A (pin labels): the fixer derived the pin order from the board itself rather than the doc (they agreed: J3 GND/3V3/SWDIO/SWCLK, J4 GND/3V3/TX/RX) and added the 4 labels that had a collision-free spot at the board's own 1.0 mm / 0.15 mm silk floor - J3 G at GND, J3 CLK at SWCLK, J4 G at GND, J4 RX at UART_RX. The other four (both 3V3 pins, SWDIO, TX) have no legal spot: the available gap below each header is <= 1.34 mm against a minimum label bounding box of 1.6965 mm in ANY orientation, with R13/C11 and the header's own reference text filling the rest. That is a physical impossibility at this pitch, not a lack of effort. MITIGATION, and it is required: both headers now carry a labelled pin 1 at one end and a labelled pin 4 at the other, which is the ordinary convention for a 0.1 in header, and the FULL pinout for J3 and J4 must appear in fab/README and the design doc so the owner can wire them without guessing. TASK B (refdes): D2 and R10 moved beside their own pads and both now pass. D1 was attempted and REVERTED - its reference text landed on D1's own body-outline silk graphic and produced a real DRC silk_overlap, and no alternative nearby spot cleared its own silk, its pads or its neighbours. R1, R2 and C10 have no legal destination at all (J1's connector pads extend past its drawn courtyard; C10 is boxed by C11/U2/C1/D1). WHY I STOP HERE RATHER THAN PUSH ON: the only remaining remedy is placement-level - moving J1, U2, R13 or C11 - which on a fully routed, DRC-perfect board means ripping copper and re-opening P6/P7 to improve four warning-severity readability findings that KiCad's own DRC does not raise at all. That trade is plainly wrong. The fixer reverting D1 rather than shipping a regression is exactly the right call and is the reason the board is still 0 violations / 0 unconnected / 0 parity. check_silk 6 -> 4; verify re-run PASS.

decisions.what: unattended default: the check_thermal waiver was RE-ISSUED at P9 against the new board digest, not carried over
decisions.why: The silk text edits changed the board, so the P8 waiver's durability binding (artifact digest 9fa76a1b + checker_version 1) stopped matching and the entry would have been surfaced as waivers_invalid rather than silently applied - the binding doing exactly the job it exists for. Re-bound to 78f20b4b after confirming the underlying finding is unchanged: the silk edits touch no copper, so the credited area, theta_JA and rise are identical, and the evidence in the reason field still holds verbatim. Re-ran the verify gate with the re-issued sidecar: PASS, 0 failing, 1 waived, 0 invalid. This will need doing again if P9's fab export or any later edit changes the board digate - the binding is deliberately fragile and must never be loosened to avoid the re-issue.

decisions.what: unattended default: CPL rotation obligation DISCHARGED - the polarity oracle checked all 26 refs with zero rotation_delta findings, and the five carried parts were confirmed individually
decisions.why: The carried P4/P8 decisions made this a REQUIRED explicit read for D1 (SOD-123 TVS), D2 and D10 (LEDs), C3 (tantalum CASE-A) and U3 (SHT40 DFN-4, added by the P8 reviewer), never to be accepted as a count - a reversed tantalum or TVS is a dead board, and a rotated DFN-4 sensor is as dead. dfm_check ran with the schematic as the polarity oracle (--schematic g0-sense.kicad_sch, the pad-geometry-vs-schematic comparison that catches the mounted-backwards class net-level parity is blind to) and reported polarity status 'checked', refs_checked 26, with NO cpl_polarity finding and therefore no rotation_delta_deg on any part. The five carried refs and their emitted CPL rotations: C3 0.0, D1 0.0, D2 180.0, D10 180.0, U3 0.0 (with J1 270.0, U1 0.0, U2 180.0 alongside). Those angles come from bom_cpl applying reference/jlc_rotations.csv per package, which is the exact KiCad-to-JLC 0-degree-reference offset the carried decision was worried about, and the oracle then re-derives each from pad geometry rather than trusting the table. Note honestly what this does and does not prove: it proves the CPL angle agrees with the schematic's pin assignment for every part, which is the machine-placement risk; it does not substitute for the owner's own first-article check on the returned boards.

decisions.what: unattended default: the single dfm warning (4 silk strokes below JLC's 0.15 mm minimum) is ACCEPTED - all four are inside U3's own DFN-4 footprint graphics
decisions.why: Located rather than counted: every sub-minimum stroke belongs to U3's footprint aiee:DFN-4_L1.5-W1.5-P0.8-TL-EP at 0.06 and 0.08 mm, a pulled easyeda2kicad body outline and pin-1 marker on a 1.5 x 1.5 mm part. The four silk texts added at P9 are NOT implicated - all sit at exactly 0.150 mm, the same as every refdes on the board, which I checked specifically because adding four labels and then seeing four sub-width strokes is too neat a coincidence to leave unverified. WHY ACCEPT: the dfm-check recipe classes silk width as advisory by design; the consequence is that U3's tiny outline may print faint or drop out, not that anything is unfabricable. WHY NOT FIX: the two available moves are both worse. Widening 0.06 mm strokes to 0.15 mm on a 1.5 mm body with 0.8 mm pitch risks pushing silk onto the pads, converting an advisory warning into a real silk_over_pad DRC error; and place_edit's silk_clear would DELETE the marker, which is the opposite of what a pin-1 indicator is for. Both require a library edit reaching an already-placed board, the P6 problem that needed a new tool. WHAT COVERS THE RESIDUAL RISK: U3's orientation is guaranteed by the CPL rotation, which the polarity oracle verified against the schematic from pad geometry - the silk is a human cross-check on a machine-placed economy-PCBA part, not the control. Note it in fab/README so the owner does not read a faint U3 outline as a placement error.
